Shri A.S. Baghel - Government Advocate for respondents/Sta
 Order

This is the first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of BNSS/439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No.205/2020 registered at Police Station Sohagpur, District Shahdol (M.P.) for the offences under Sections 376(2)(n), 376(2(f),
376(3), 506 of IPC and Section 3/4 & 5(L)(6)/5(n), 6 of POCSO 2012 and 3(2)(va) of SC & ST Act.
It is submitted that the applicant has falsely been implicated in the case and he has not committed any offence in any manner.
He is ready to abide by all the terms and conditions that may be imposed by this Court while considering the bail application.
On these grounds, he prays for grant of bail.

Per contra, learned counsel appearing for the State as well as counsel has vehemently opposed the application stating that there is specific allegation against the applicant made by the prosecutrix in her statements NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:60340 2 MCRC-49006-2024 recorded under Sections 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C. Applicant being the step father.
The prosecutrix was only 13 years of age at the time of commission of offence.
He prays for dismissal of bail application.
Considering the overall circumstances of the case, as well as the fact that the custody period in such heinous offence cannot be the sole ground for grant of bail.

The role of the applicant in the present Kamal Prajapati vs State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109898623/
1 matter is clearly reflected by the prosecution which is duly supported by the statement of the prosecutrix, this Court does not deem it appropriate to enlarge the applicant on bail.
